user.title: Add a TV
user.description:
**Samsung:** enable Developer Mode on the TV, set its **Host PC IP** to the IP address of this Home Assistant and restart the TV.

**LG:** install the **Developer Mode** app from the LG Content Store, sign in with an LG developer account and turn **Dev Mode Status** on.

data_description.host: The TV must be on and in Developer Mode.

webos.title: LG TV: Developer Mode key
webos.description: On the TV open the **Developer Mode** app, switch **Key Server** on and type the **passphrase** shown on the screen (6 characters). Home Assistant downloads the key from {host} once; afterwards you can switch Key Server off.

reauth_confirm.title: LG TV: new Developer Mode key
reauth_confirm.description: The TV {name} no longer accepts the stored key (Developer Mode was reinstalled or switched off and on). Open the **Developer Mode** app, switch **Key Server** on and type the new passphrase.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to the TV. Check that it is on, Developer Mode is enabled and Host PC IP is set to this Home Assistant's IP address.
error.key_server: The Key Server on the TV is not reachable. Open the Developer Mode app on the TV and switch Key Server on.
error.cannot_connect_webos: The TV does not accept SSH connections on port 9922. Check that Dev Mode Status is on.

abort.wrong_tv: This is a different TV (serial number does not match).

user.title: Signing certificate
user.description: Create a new certificate with your Samsung account, or upload one you already have. An installed app can only be updated with **the same author certificate** it was installed with.

tizenbrew.title: TizenBrew Installer certificate
tizenbrew.description: Upload `tizenbrewInstallerConfig.json` (found in `%USERPROFILE%\share\` on the computer where TizenBrew Installer ran).

p12.title: PKCS#12 certificate pair
p12.description: Upload `author.p12` and `distributor.p12` (Apps2Samsung: `%APPDATA%\Apps2Samsung\Certificate\` (one folder per profile), password is in `password.txt`).

samsung.title: New certificate (Samsung account)
samsung.description: The certificate will be issued for these TVs: **{duids}**. On the next page you sign in with your Samsung account; you need a computer in the same network. A free account is enough: {account_url}.

data_description.author_cn: Shown in the certificate. Anything, e.g. your name.
data_description.privilege: Public is enough for almost all apps. Partner only for apps that say they need it.
data_description.extra_duids: Optional: DUIDs of Samsung TVs that are not in HA-Brew, separated by commas.

error.invalid_cert: The certificate could not be opened (wrong file or password).
error.wrong_device: This distributor certificate was not issued for this TV (DUID does not match).
error.too_many_duids: Samsung allows at most 50 TVs per certificate.
error.no_duid: No TV to issue the certificate for.

abort.samsung_timeout: No sign-in arrived within 15 minutes. Start again.
abort.samsung_rate_limited: Samsung refused: too many requests. Try again in an hour.
abort.samsung_no_email: Your Samsung account has no e-mail address. Add one at {profile_url} and try again.
abort.samsung_auth: Samsung did not accept the sign-in ({error}). Start again.

progress.samsung_login:
**On a computer in the same network as Home Assistant**, run this command (it opens the Samsung sign-in in the browser and passes the result to Home Assistant):

**Windows** – press Win + R, paste, press Enter:
```
{windows}
```

**macOS / Linux** – in Terminal:
```
{unix}
```

Then sign in with your Samsung account in the browser. This dialog continues by itself (waits up to 15 minutes).

user.title: Add app
user.description: Choose a known app or a custom GitHub repository. Samsung: also the certificate the app was installed with.

data_description.asset_pattern: Which file of a release to install, e.g. `\.wgt$` (Samsung) or `\.ipk$` (LG).

error.no_asset: No release of this repository contains a matching file.
error.github_error: GitHub could not be reached or the repository does not exist.

abort.no_certificates: Add a signing certificate to this TV first.

options.entity: Turn on an entity (e.g. samsungtv_smart, webostv)

no_release.message: No release of {app} is known yet. Wait for the next check or check the repository.

certificate_missing.message: The certificate of this app was removed. Reconfigure the app.

certificate_invalid.message: The signing certificate could not be used: {error}

install_author_mismatch.message: The TV refused the update: the app was installed with a different author certificate than "{certificate}". Use the certificate the app was originally installed with.

install_certificate.message: The TV rejected the signature ({error}). The certificate may have expired or was not issued for this TV.

install_platform.message: This package is not compatible with the TV's Tizen version ({error}).

tv_unreachable.message: The TV is not reachable. Turn it on and make sure Developer Mode is enabled ({error}).

install_running.message: An installation of this app is already running.

download_failed.message: The package could not be downloaded: {error}

checksum_mismatch.message: The downloaded package does not match the catalog checksum and was not installed.

wake_failed.message: The TV did not wake up in time. Check the wake-up settings and that Developer Mode is enabled.

launch_failed.message: The TV could not start the app: {error}

auth_failed.message: The TV rejected the Developer Mode key. Open the integration and enter the new passphrase ({error}).

devmode_failed.message: The Developer Mode session could not be extended: {error}

uninstall_failed.message: The TV did not remove the app ({error}). Some TVs do not allow this; remove it on the TV: Apps → select the app → Delete.

platform_too_old.message: This package needs {os} {required} or newer; the TV runs {os} {current}.

init.title: Wake-up
init.description: How HA-Brew turns the TV on before installing or launching an app. Developer Mode must stay enabled.

data_description.wake_entity: For example the media player of Samsung TV Smart (samsungtv_smart) or LG webOS TV (webostv).

devmode_expiring.title: Developer Mode on {tv} is running out
devmode_expiring.description:
About {hours} hours are left in the LG Developer Mode session. When it runs out, the TV removes every app installed in Developer Mode (Homebrew Channel, Nuvio, …). HA-Brew extends the session automatically once a day; this did not work ({error}).

Turn the TV on, open the **Developer Mode** app and press **Extend**, or press **Extend Developer Mode** on the TV's device page. If the app shows that Dev Mode is off, sign in again and switch it on.
